title: Temporal Enhanced Training of Multi-view 3D Object Detector via Historical Object Prediction (HoP)
text: Train-only auxiliary task: build a pseudo BEV feature for t-k from the other frames WITHOUT the images of t-k (short-term and long-term deformable decoders) and predict the objects at t-k. nuScenes val R50: BEVFormer-opt 51.3 to 53.1 NDS, BEVDet4D-Depth 49.3 to 50.9; predicting the FUTURE frame t+1 gives 52.3 against 53.1 for t-1; k = 2, 3 give 53.4 / 53.6 at 2.3x memory; not detaching the history gives 53.9 at about +10 % time. Cost +5 % (BEVDet4D) to +20 % (BEVFormer) training time, none at inference. Single runs, loss weight unreported.
idea: past-target decode at dt = -0.5 as a loss from week one; budget extra decoded times by memory (k > 1 doubles it); detaching history costs 0.8 NDS

title: MapTCL: Temporal Consistency Learning via Bidirectional Alignment for Vectorized HD Map Construction (IROS 2026)
text: Train-only consistency loss between the current prediction and ego-warped past predictions in both directions (vector level plus a raster level focal loss between current and warped past raster maps; per-frame weights falling with age: 9/7/5/3/1 and 1/0.7/0.5/0.3/0.1). nuScenes new split mAP 35.2 to 38.9 on StreamMapNet (+3.7); forward-only 35.9 vs bidirectional 37.2; memory 5 frames best on Argoverse2 (56.7 mAP), 7 frames worse (51.6); no overlap or occlusion mask; no inference cost. No code.
idea: raster consistency loss with the splat as the warp, both directions, per-age weights, plus our mass and visibility masks; limit the window to about 5 frames

title: ST-P3: End-to-end Vision-based Autonomous Driving via Spatial-Temporal Feature Learning (ECCV 2022) with the FIERY loss recipe
text: Future prediction with a dual-pathway GRU (history path plus latent path); loss at ALL future time steps with an exponential discount (+0.47 IoU / +0.37 PQ over the last step only, vehicle IoU 38.16 to 38.63). Horizon 1 s past + 2 s future at 2 Hz, Adam lr 2e-4 constant, 20 epochs, mixed precision, 4 V100. FIERY (read for the loss): discount gamma = 0.95 per step, Kendall weights on seg / centerness / offset / flow, KL weight 100, Adam 3e-4 batch 12; removing the ego-motion transform costs 6.4 IoU (short range) at 2 s. No gamma ablation in either paper.
idea: published future-loss discount is mild (0.95 per 0.5 s step) against our 0.5; make the dt weight an arm (0.5 vs 0.9)

title: UnFlow: Unsupervised Learning of Optical Flow with a Bidirectional Census Loss (AAAI 2018)
text: Forward and backward flow with an occlusion mask from the forward-backward check (|f_fwd + f_bwd warped|^2 > 0.01 (|f_fwd|^2 + |f_bwd|^2) + 0.5); data and consistency terms masked by (1 - occluded), a constant penalty per occluded pixel prevents the all-occluded solution. KITTI 2012 / 2015 training-set error 4.32 / 9.17 with masking and no consistency term, 3.78 / 8.80 with the consistency term lambda_C = 0.2 (about 12 % / 4 %). Photometric census terms are not our setting.
idea: cycle check between the dt and -dt velocity fields with a masked loss plus a constant penalty for masked cells; adaptation to BEV is ours, not in the paper

title: An Efficient Occupancy World Model via Decoupled Dynamic Flow and Image-assisted Training (DFIT-OccWorld)
text: Forecast by grid_sample of existing features with a predicted flow (dynamic voxels) and by the ego pose alone (static voxels), single training stage, all futures at once. nuScenes 1-3 s average: direct baseline 18.97 mIoU / 28.44 IoU; + flow decoder 20.67 / 29.89; + decoupled dynamic flow 20.89 / 30.97; OccWorld 17.14 / 26.63; render-based photometric consistency adds more (21.96 alone). Training 25.1 h against 66.7 h for OccWorld. Loss weights and any flow loss not given; no code.
idea: evidence that warping the state with a learned flow beats decoding the future from scratch (+1.7 mIoU); static by pose, dynamic by flow

title: Streaming Map Network (StreamMapNet): streaming BEV memory for online vectorized HD maps
text: BEV memory warped by the ego-pose transform and fused with a GRU plus LayerNorm; gradients do not propagate into the previous frames; each sequence is split at a random point every epoch; 4 epochs of single-frame training first. Argoverse2 new split mAP: query propagation 42.8, + transformation loss 43.7, + BEV fusion 46.1. AdamW 5e-4, batch 32 on 8 x 3090, 24 epochs on nuScenes; 13.2 FPS. Frames per sample and memory initialisation not stated.
idea: recipe for a recurrent BEV memory: detach, single-frame warm-up, random sequence cut, GRU with LayerNorm; transformation loss as the instance-level consistency

title: What Matters for Scalable and Robust Learning in End-to-End Driving Planners? (BevAD, CVPR Findings 2026)
text: Compute-frugal 2026 recipe of a BEV driving planner: Schedule-Free AdamW (wd 0.01), bf16 mixed precision, 4-epoch BEV-backbone warm-up with perception loss then planning with the backbone frozen, recurrent BEV generation replaced by cached features streamed from 20-frame snippets (about 2 s) with periodic memory reset; 100 x 100 BEV; 570 A100-80GB hours (about 10x less than ParaDrive); batch 16 on a single A100-80GB in the appendix. No optimiser or precision ablation; lr and detach not stated.
idea: bf16 + schedule-free optimiser + streamed 2 s snippets as the three cheap choices for one card

title: UniBEV: Multi-modal 3D Object Detection with Uniform BEV Encoders for Robustness against Missing Sensor Modalities
text: Modality dropout with numbers (camera-LiDAR): with p = 0.5 one modality's BEV features are dropped (LiDAR kept 0.5, camera 0.5, so 50 % both, 25 % each alone); channel-wise softmax-weighted averaging fusion. nuScenes val mAP for L+C / L / C: default 64.2 / 58.2 / 35.0; with camera-only never trained (p_C = 0) camera-only collapses to 3.0 mAP while the fused score stays 60.8. No run without dropout, optimiser not stated, 36 epochs on 4 x A40. Radar not tested.
idea: separate drop rates per sensor; a sensor never seen alone is useless alone; check clean accuracy against a no-dropout control

title: Can BEV Perception Gracefully Degrade under Sensor Failures? (TrustGate router, three-phase training)
text: On BEVFusion-MIT plain modality dropout (both 0.5, each alone 0.25) cost 10.8 mAP of clean accuracy (66.9 to 56.1; NDS 69.7 to 62.2) and left the LiDAR-drop case at 12.1 mAP; with a TrustGate router and a 3-phase schedule (1 epoch vision warm-up lr 1e-4; 3 epochs router + fusion with dropout, backbones frozen, lr 1e-5; 3 epochs end-to-end without dropout, lr 1e-7) clean 68.3, LiDAR-drop 32.8, camera-drop 58.4 mAP. Camera-LiDAR, single runs, no code.
idea: dropout can hurt clean accuracy: stage it (warm-up, dropout phase, low-lr no-dropout end) and gate it against a no-dropout control

title: BEVDet: High-performance Multi-camera 3D Object Detection in Bird-Eye-View
text: Augmentation in BEV space (flip, rotation +-22.5 deg, scale 0.95-1.05 on the view transformer output and the targets) is what regularises the BEV encoder and head: nuScenes val mAP final epoch none 17.4, image-view aug only 17.8, BEV aug only 23.6, both 31.2. Recipe: AdamW 2e-4, batch 64 on 8 x 3090, 20 epochs, CBGS; config dev2.1: wd 1e-7, clip 5, warm-up 200 it, EMA, with_cp. Scale-NMS 29.5 to 31.2 mAP. Licence not stated.
idea: BDA applied to the BEV tensor, targets, ego motion, Doppler vectors and every frame of a sequence identically; flip only as an arm (driving side)

title: Training recipes read from the configs of BEVFormer, StreamPETR, BEVDet, CRT-Fusion, RaCFormer, CR3DT, Simple-BEV
text: One table: AdamW everywhere; lr 2e-4 to 4e-4 for batches of 8 to 64 (not linearly scaled); wd 0.01 (transformers) or 1e-7 (BEVDet family); pretrained backbone lr x 0.1; warm-up 200-500 it; cosine to 1e-3 of peak; clip 5-35; EMA in the BEVDet family; fp16 with dynamic loss scale; with_cp on backbone and decoder; history detached, StreamPETR gradients through one frame; first phase without history (CRT-Fusion 6 epochs); CR3DT trains radar-camera on ONE RTX 3090 with gradient accumulation 8. EMA (BEVDepth / BEVStereo README table, MIT): +0.1 to +1.5 mAP, -0.1 to +1.0 NDS. Proposal for a 3060 is marked as inference.
idea: start recipe for the 3060: AdamW 2e-4, accumulate to batch 16, warm-up 500 it from lr/3, cosine to 1e-3, clip 5, EMA 0.999, phase 1 dt = 0 without history

title: PyTorch autocast (bf16 / fp16), channels_last, torch.compile and activation checkpointing: what is documented and what it means for the splat
text: Docs 2.9 list grid_sample, index_put and scatter_add under promote-to-widest-input, so float32 coordinates keep the splat in float32 even with bf16 features; the page does not say whether the lists hold for bf16. channels_last: over 22 % for ResNet-50 AMP training on Tensor Core GPUs. torch.compile: 43 % average training speed-up on an A100 over 163 models, lower on desktop GPUs, limited with dynamic shapes. Checkpointing (Chen et al.): 1000-layer ResNet 48 GB to 7 GB at about +30 % time. bf16 coordinates at 32-64 m have 0.25 m spacing (our arithmetic).
idea: never cast positions / mass / v dt to bf16; compile only fixed-shape trunk and heads; checkpoint the K-source window if memory demands

title: Class-balanced Grouping and Sampling for Point Cloud 3D Object Detection (CBGS)
text: nuScenes val (sparse-conv LiDAR detector): class-balanced sampling (10 % of 128,106 sample counts per class, epoch 4.5x longer) adds 4.95 mAP / 3.0 NDS on top of GT augmentation (37.69 to 42.64), multi-head grouping of similar classes +2.2 mAP. Table header says DB sampling while the text says DS sampling. AdamW one-cycle max lr 0.04, batch 5, 20 epochs. No code on the page.
idea: oversample frames with rare class groups (two-wheelers) as a partial arm; the epoch length grows in proportion

title: OccProphet: Pushing Efficiency Frontier of Camera-Only 4D Occupancy Forecasting with Observer-Forecaster-Refiner Framework (ICLR 2025)
text: Occupancy forecasting on reduced-resolution features: against Cam4DOcc 82 M vs 370 M parameters, training memory 24 vs 57 GB, 1985 vs 6434 GFLOPs, 4.5 vs 1.7 FPS, future IoU 29.15 vs 27.98. 3 input frames, 4 future frames at 2 Hz, 0.2 m voxels 512 x 512 x 40; AdamW 3e-4, batch 4 on 4 x RTX 4090; loss as Cam4DOcc (not given). The paper's tables disagree with each other in places.
idea: efficiency baseline for forecasting; our 2D 0.5 m grid has about 840x fewer cells than its voxel grid

title: The Road Less Scheduled (Schedule-Free AdamW)
text: Optimiser that removes the learning-rate schedule and the need to know the stopping step T; no extra hyperparameter; core of a winning AlgoPerf 2024 self-tuning entry (abstract); claims to match or beat tuned cosine schedules on 28 problems (authors' evaluation, search snippet). BEV-side use found: BevAD 2603.15185 (no ablation). Averaged weights are used for evaluation; BatchNorm statistics need care (memory).
idea: optimiser arm for runs of open length (dt warm-up and dropout start do not depend on a cosine horizon); equal-budget control against AdamW + cosine

title: Planning-oriented Autonomous Driving (UniAD)
text: Read on ar5iv: two-stage training, stage 1 tracking + mapping 6 epochs from pretrained BEVFormer weights, stage 2 end-to-end 20 epochs (called more stable); occupancy module predicts T_o = 5 time steps (IoU-near 61.2 to 62.6, VPQ-near 51.5 to 53.2 with the full OccFormer design). Optimiser details and the gradient handling of history were in the truncated part of the page. Code public, licence not stated on the page.
idea: staged training pattern (perception first, then the temporal and prediction heads)

title: Driving in the Occupancy World: Vision-Centric 4D Occupancy Forecasting and Planning via World Models (Drive-OccWorld)
text: Digest only (search result): auto-regressive forecasting of future occupancy and flow with an occupancy-based planner. Training losses and horizon schedule not read.
idea: not read; candidate for occupancy-flow loss weights

title: CycleBEV: Regularizing View Transformation Networks via View Cycle Consistency for BEV Semantic Segmentation
text: Train-only inverse view transformation (BEV map back to perspective-view map) used as a cycle-consistency regulariser; on four view-transformation models on nuScenes gains up to 0.74 mIoU drivable, 4.86 vehicle, 3.74 pedestrian; no inference cost. A spatial (view) cycle, not a temporal one; the camera heads are frozen in our design.
idea: cycle regulariser pattern with zero inference cost
extract: skip: spatial cycle with frozen camera heads

title: OccWorld: Learning a 3D Occupancy World Model for Autonomous Driving (ECCV 2024)
text: Digest (search result and DFIT-OccWorld): two stages, scene tokenizer and decoder trained with a softmax plus Lovasz-softmax occupancy loss, then a generative transformer for future tokens and ego displacement; DFIT-OccWorld reports 66.7 h training for it against 25.1 h single-stage. Not read.
idea: the two-stage baseline that DFIT-OccWorld improves on

title: HorizonDrive: Self-Corrective Autoregressive World Model for Long-horizon Driving Simulation
text: Digest (search result): video generation world model; a scheduled rollout recovery step trains on prediction-corrupted histories. The closest hit for scheduled sampling / horizon curriculum; none found for BEV maps or boxes.
idea: none for dense BEV maps

title: DREAMSTEER: Latent World Models Can Steer VLA Policies During Deployment Without Any Finetuning
text: Digest (search result): latent world model for a VLA policy, alternates teacher-forcing and sampling losses with a scheduled curriculum. Not a BEV model.
idea: none
